prerequisites: Knowledge in the breadth of the studied subject

learning_outcomes.text: Students can methodically process practical tasks and present them within a given timeframe with a clearly structured result.

Students possess a critical understanding of the most important theories, principles, and methods from their studies, can on this basis familiarize themselves with a new task, and independently deepen their knowledge in a special area.
Students can evaluate the state of literature in the context of the underlying research question and critically reflect on methodological approaches.

Students use the tools and methods learned and developed during their studies to support their work. They develop solution approaches based on these and thus realize solutions corresponding to the state of science.

Students research the state of the art and science and derive innovative approaches for the specific scientific task of their thesis. In their explanations, they present the underlying research results and their innovations.

Students formulate identified technical challenges and solutions, categorize them into an interdisciplinary context, and present them in discourse with subject matter experts. They communicate with stakeholders and consider their diverse perspectives and interests.

In their thesis, students develop a professional self-image that is oriented towards the goals and standards of professional action in professional fields primarily outside of science. They recognize situational framework conditions of professional action in relation to the task of their thesis and can reflect on their activity in an interdisciplinary context.

syllabus_topics: Recording the state of the art
Creation of concepts for solving the task
Development of partial solutions and assembly into an overall concept
Overall consideration and evaluation of the solution
Presentation of the solution in the form of the Bachelor thesis
Presentation of the results within a colloquium
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance consists of the thesis and the colloquium. 12 ECTS points are awarded for the Bachelor thesis and 3 ECTS points for the colloquium. The Bachelor thesis is 40-70 pages long. The colloquium is 15-45 minutes long.
